aave.LongDescription: Aave is an overcollateralised, pooled money market: lenders deposit assets into shared reserves and borrowers draw against collateral they have posted, with interest rates set algorithmically by pool utilisation rather than by a credit committee. Since [Aave V3 shipped on 16 March 2022](https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog) the protocol has layered risk controls on top of that base: efficiency mode, isolation mode, and supply and borrow caps per asset. [Aave V4 went live on Ethereum mainnet on 30 March 2026](https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog) with a hub-and-spoke design in which a Liquidity Hub holds assets centrally and Spokes connect to it with their own collateral types, risk parameters and liquidation rules, deployed initially as three hubs (Core, Plus, Prime) and eleven spokes. Loans are perpetual with no fixed maturity; positions are liquidated by third-party liquidators when the health factor breaches its threshold, and Aave states it has [liquidated more than $4.4B safely with zero bad debt across six-plus years of uninterrupted operation](https://aave.com/security). Users span retail leverage, market-neutral basis traders, treasuries, and, through [Horizon](https://aave.com/blog/horizon-launch), institutions borrowing stablecoins against permissioned tokenised RWA collateral.

Faq.question: Has Aave taken bad debt?
Faq.answer: Aave's own security page claims more than $4.4B liquidated safely with zero bad debt across six-plus years of operation ([Aave security page](https://aave.com/security)). Chaos Labs, the outgoing risk manager, independently stated that during its tenure Aave processed over $2B in liquidations with zero material bad debt while growing from $5.2B to more than $26B in TVL ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/chaos-labs-terminates-aave-engagement-citing-risk-misalignment)). Aave v3.3 nonetheless added explicit logging and burn functionality to manage undercollateralised borrow positions, which is an admission that residual dust debt exists and needs handling ([Aave changelog](https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog)).

Faq.question: Who sets interest rates and risk parameters?
Faq.answer: Rates follow a per-reserve utilisation curve whose parameters are changed only by an Aave Improvement Proposal voted on-chain by AAVE holders, with a mandatory timelock of one day for standard changes and seven days for governance changes ([Aave security page](https://aave.com/security)). Historically the parameter recommendations came from external risk managers, principally Chaos Labs and LlamaRisk, working through the governance forum ([Chaos Labs monthly community update](https://governance.aave.com/t/chaos-labs-monthly-community-update/11174/36)). With Chaos Labs gone as of April 2026, LlamaRisk has proposed to take on continuity of that function ([LlamaRisk continuity proposal](https://governance.aave.com/t/llamarisk-ensuring-continuity-of-aaves-risk-management/24397)).

Faq.question: How does liquidation work?
Faq.answer: Positions become liquidatable when the health factor breaches its threshold and any third party can repay debt in exchange for discounted collateral. V4 moves liquidation rules down to the Spoke level, so each Spoke carries its own collateral types, risk parameters and liquidation rules rather than inheriting one global configuration ([Aave V4 live](https://aave.com/blog/aave-v4-live-ethereum)). Aave has liquidated more than $4.4B cumulatively ([Aave security page](https://aave.com/security)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: A smart contract failure or an oracle failure that lets a position drain a reserve. Aave mitigates with 65 audits, formal verification by Certora, a 5-of-9 Guardian veto during timelock, and the Umbrella backstop holding $148.41M ([Aave security page](https://aave.com/security)). The second-order worst case is governance: DL News describes a protracted power struggle in which ACI alleged that the largest DAO budget vote was backed almost entirely by addresses linked to Aave Labs ([DL News](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/aave-firm-exits-defi-giant-amid-protracted-power-struggle/)).

Faq.question: What is Horizon and does it change the credit profile?
Faq.answer: Horizon is an Aave-licensed institutional instance built on Aave Protocol v3.3 where permissioned RWA collateral (Superstate USTB and USCC, Centrifuge JTRSY and JAAA, Circle USYC coming) backs permissionless supply of RLUSD, USDC and GHO; aTokens for RWA collateral are non-transferable and issuers control whitelisting and KYC ([Aave Horizon](https://aave.com/blog/horizon-launch)). It introduces issuer and legal-wrapper risk that does not exist in the crypto-collateral pools. Reported deposits reached $550M ([BlockEden](https://blockeden.xyz/blog/2026/04/21/aave-horizon-550m-institutional-rwa-deposits-permissioned-defi-tradfi/)).

Faq.question: How far along is V4 adoption?
Faq.answer: V4 launched 30 March 2026 ([Aave changelog](https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog)) and had surpassed $200M in total deposits by the June 2026 update, with a Paxos Hub live, Avalanche and Arc activations in preparation, and an AIP submitted for V3 on Monad ([AL Development Update June 2026](https://governance.aave.com/t/al-development-update-june-2026/25266)). Against $13.78B in V3 ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/aave-v3)), migration is at an early stage.

Faq.question: Is the governance dispute resolved?
Faq.answer: Not fully. The IP transfer proposal failed on 25 December 2025, BGD Labs exited in February 2026, ACI announced its wind-down on 3 March 2026, and the $25M Labs grant passed on 12 April 2026 ([DL News](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/aave-firm-exits-defi-giant-amid-protracted-power-struggle/), [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/397138/aave-dao-approves-25-million-aave-labs-funding-grant-in-binding-aave-will-win-vote)). ACI stated it saw no role for an independent service provider where the largest budget recipient holds undisclosed voting power and uses it on its own proposals ([DL News](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/aave-firm-exits-defi-giant-amid-protracted-power-struggle/)).

bull.claim: Scale and share are unmatched: $14.35B TVL with $11.01B borrowed as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama), and Aave states it has processed over one trillion dollars in cumulative loans while holding more than 50% of the decentralised lending market (Aave V4 live).
Credit track record is the best in the sector: more than $4.4B liquidated with zero bad debt over six-plus years, plus a $148.41M Umbrella backstop (Aave security page).

Security spend is real, not nominal: 65 audits, Certora formal verification across Hub, Spoke and Libraries, a SOC-2 Type II in March 2026, and zero high-severity findings across 345 days of review and a 900-participant public contest for the V4 governance update (Aave security page).

Institutional distribution is live rather than theoretical: Horizon spans Ant Digital Technologies, Chainlink, Ethena, KAIO, OpenEden, Ripple, Securitize, VanEck and WisdomTree (Aave Horizon) and reportedly reached $550M in RWA deposits (BlockEden).

bear.claim: The independent risk layer has been dismantled inside six months: BGD Labs out in February 2026, ACI winding down from 3 March 2026, Chaos Labs terminated in April 2026 after pricing every loan since November 2022 (DL News, The Defiant).

The risk-budget gap is quantified and unresolved: Aave Labs offered to raise the risk budget to $5M while Chaos Labs estimated $8M minimum was required to cover a V4 codebase it described as entirely new, with Risk Oracle infrastructure that cannot be ported (The Defiant).

Governance capture is an explicit allegation from an insider: ACI alleged the largest budget vote in DAO history was backed almost entirely by addresses linked to Aave Labs, and a proposal to move IP to the DAO was defeated (DL News).
The token has de-rated hard against the fundamentals: AAVE traded near $96 in April 2026, down roughly 73% from an August 2025 high of $356 (The Defiant).

compound.LongDescription: Compound is the original algorithmic money market: users supply assets to a pool, interest rates adjust in real time with utilisation, and borrowers post collateral to draw funds. Compound III, codenamed Comet, replaced the pooled-risk model of v2 with a one-base-asset-per-market design in which each deployment supports a single borrowable base asset and a list of collateral assets that cannot themselves be borrowed and earn no interest ([Compound docs](https://docs.compound.finance/collateral-and-borrowing/)). Borrowing capacity comes from a per-collateral `borrowCollateralFactor`, capped by a per-asset `supplyCap`, with a `baseBorrowMin` floor on position size and signed base-token balances where positive means supplied and negative means borrowed ([Compound docs](https://docs.compound.finance/collateral-and-borrowing/)). Loans are perpetual and liquidation is via `absorb()`, which transfers collateral to protocol reserves at a discount ([Eco](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14800897-compound-v3-comet-architecture-deep-dive)). Users are mostly stablecoin borrowers seeking leverage on blue-chip collateral, plus COMP-incentivised suppliers.

Faq.question: Has Compound taken bad debt?
Faq.answer: No aggregate bad-debt figure is published in the fetched sources, so `n.a.` for a protocol-level number. What is documented is that Comet's `absorb()` function moves underwater collateral into protocol reserves and credits the protocol with base asset, meaning shortfalls land on the reserve rather than on individual suppliers ([Eco](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14800897-compound-v3-comet-architecture-deep-dive)). Compound also used governance in May 2026 to liquidate a hacker's collateral position directly ([Santiment](https://app.santiment.net/insights/read/deep-dive-how-defi-governance-liquidated-the-kelpdao-hacker-s-collateral-on-compound-10841)).

Faq.question: Who sets rates and risk parameters?
Faq.answer: COMP holders and delegates, executing through the mainnet Timelock which administers every community-sanctioned Compound III instance ([Compound governance docs](https://docs.compound.finance/governance/)). Parameter recommendations come from Gauntlet, whose 2024 renewal covered 25 Comets at $2.3M per year ([comp.xyz](https://www.comp.xyz/t/gauntlet-compound-renewal-2024/5661)). The DAO has debated the concentration this creates, including a March 2025 thread on the pressing need for a secondary risk manager ([comp.xyz](https://www.comp.xyz/t/dao-ops-concerns-the-pressing-need-for-a-secondary-risk-manager/6448/4)).

Faq.question: How does liquidation work in Comet?
Faq.answer: Each account's health is evaluated with `isBorrowCollateralized` and `isLiquidatable` against per-collateral liquidation factors ([Compound docs](https://docs.compound.finance/collateral-and-borrowing/)). If the account is liquidatable, anyone can call `absorb()`, which transfers the collateral to protocol reserves at a discount and credits the protocol with the base asset ([Eco](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14800897-compound-v3-comet-architecture-deep-dive)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: Contract failure in a market where their base asset sits, or a governance action that changes parameters against them, since the Timelock can reconfigure any Comet ([Compound governance docs](https://docs.compound.finance/governance/)). The July 2024 Golden Boys episode showed that a coordinated whale can pass a proposal moving $24M of DAO assets before a truce is negotiated ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/308215/compound-reaches-truce-with-crypto-whale-humpy-after-controversial-vote-to-move-24-million-in-tokens)). Mitigants are Trail of Bits and OpenZeppelin audits plus Certora formal verification wired into CI ([Compound security](https://compound.finance/docs/security)).

Faq.question: Why is collateral non-yielding in Compound III?
Faq.answer: By design: collateral assets do not earn interest and exist purely as backing, which is what allows higher borrowing capacity with lower liquidation risk and lower gas ([Compound docs](https://docs.compound.finance/collateral-and-borrowing/)). Leshner framed the trade at launch as borrowing more, with less liquidation risk, lower penalties and less gas, at the cost of collateral yield ([CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/compound-v3-comet-launched-with-support-for-single-borrowing-model/)).

Faq.question: How much of the market has Compound lost?
Faq.answer: Compound V3 held $1.139B TVL on 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/compound-v3)) against Aave's $14.35B ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/aave)) and Morpho Blue's $7.52B ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/morpho-blue)). The Defiant ran a February 2026 piece explicitly asking what happened to Compound's lending empire ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/what-happened-to-compound-defi-lender)).

bull.claim: The Comet architecture materially reduces contagion: each base-asset market is isolated so collateral held against a USDC loan cannot cross-contaminate a separate ETH market, with per-market collateral factors set through a single Configurator (Ancilar).

Verification depth is unusual: the protocol was developed against a specification of security principles and formally verified by Certora using Certora ASA, integrated into continuous integration rather than run once (Compound security).
Governance is deep and liquid: 21.15K delegates, 220.32K token holders and 548 proposals on Tally (Tally), now supported by a funded Foundation with a $6M annual budget (comp.xyz).
Distribution is genuinely multi-chain: nine chains carry Comet deployments including Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Scroll, Mantle, Unichain and Ronin (DefiLlama).

bear.claim: Compound is now a distant third: $1.14B TVL versus Aave's $14.35B and Morpho Blue's $7.52B on the same day (DefiLlama V3, DefiLlama Aave, DefiLlama Morpho Blue).

Governance capture has already been attempted successfully once: the Golden Boys passed a $24M treasury proposal in July 2024 before a truce, with COMP falling sharply in the aftermath (The Block, CoinDesk).

Single-risk-manager dependency is acknowledged inside the DAO, with a March 2025 thread on the need for a secondary risk manager and an August 2025 thread arguing against re-hiring Gauntlet at all (comp.xyz, comp.xyz).
Founder and product-line attrition: Leshner left in 2023 to found Superstate and Compound Treasury was shut down, leaving the protocol without its original commercial engine (The Defiant, Axios).

morpho.LongDescription: Morpho unbundles lending into an immutable primitive plus an external curation layer. A Morpho variable-rate market (Morpho Blue) pairs exactly one collateral asset with one loan asset and fixes four parameters at creation, the oracle, the interest rate model, the LLTV and the two assets, after which they persist in perpetuity; market creation is permissionless and requires no governance vote, though the LLTV and IRM must be drawn from governance-approved sets ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/market/)). Governance-approved LLTVs are 0, 38.5, 62.5, 77.0, 86.0, 91.5, 94.5, 96.5 and 98.0 percent, and the only approved IRM is AdaptiveCurveIRM ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/market/)). Because each market is isolated and immutable, risk selection moves to vault curators: MetaMorpho and Vaults V2 allocate depositor funds across markets, so the depositor is really buying a curator's credit judgment. In 2026 Morpho added a fixed-rate, fixed-term protocol, Midnight, launched on Base in July 2026, in which lenders and borrowers propose their own rates and maturities instead of relying on a utilisation curve ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/347128040805697)).

Faq.question: Has Morpho taken bad debt?
Faq.answer: Yes, at the vault level. After the Stream Finance deUSD collapse on 8 November 2025, Morpho delisted the Elixir sdeUSD/USDC market and the affected MEV Capital vault carried roughly 3.6% bad debt, with deUSD falling from $1 to $0.11 and about $500M of market cap evaporating across Euler, Morpho and Silo ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/32330428064082)). Analysts subsequently mapped roughly $285M of potential exposure across DeFi from the same event ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/377491/analysts-map-285m-in-potential-exposure-across-defi-after-stream-finances-93m-loss)). The protocol itself has no shared pool to socialise those losses, which is the design intent.

Faq.question: Who sets rates and risk parameters?
Faq.answer: Nobody centrally. Each market's IRM and LLTV are chosen at creation from governance-approved sets and are immutable thereafter, with AdaptiveCurveIRM the only approved model and nine approved LLTV values ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/market/)). Governance can whitelist new LLTVs and IRMs and flip a fee switch capped at 25% of borrower interest, but cannot change a live market ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/governance/organization/)). Effective risk selection is made by vault curators.

Faq.question: Who is actually the credit underwriter I am relying on?
Faq.answer: The vault curator. At launch these were Steakhouse Financial, Block Analitica and B.Protocol ([Morpho LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/morpho-labs_movetomorpho-activity-7150863577116012545-n8Yy)), and by April 2026 the set included the Ethereum Foundation, Gauntlet and Steakhouse ([Real World Tokenspace](https://www.realworldtokenspace.com/research/2026-04-24-morpho-vaults-ethereum-foundation-gauntlet-steakhouse-curators)). Morpho's own documentation includes explicit curator security considerations and a bad-debt handling guide ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/concepts/security-considerations/), [Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/curate/tutorials-v1/bad-debt/)).

Faq.question: How does liquidation work?
Faq.answer: If a borrower's position exceeds the market LLTV, anyone can liquidate it by repaying a portion of the debt in exchange for a discounted portion of the collateral ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/market/)). The liquidation incentive factor formula is not stated on that page, so `n.a.` for the exact discount schedule.

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: A curator allocating into a market whose collateral asset breaks and whose oracle keeps pricing it, which is exactly the Stream Finance pattern: the loss lands entirely inside that vault ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/32330428064082)). Contract risk is mitigated by audits from Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, ChainSecurity, Certora, Zellic and Blackthorn ([Morpho audits](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/resources/audits/)) and a $2.5M Cantina bounty ([Cantina](https://cantina.xyz/bounties/35a5f0a1-2ffd-432c-8f3b-77d169add8c3)), but curator risk cannot be audited away.

Faq.question: What is Midnight and how is it different from Blue?
Faq.answer: Midnight is Morpho's fixed-rate, fixed-term protocol, live on Base mainnet from July 2026 with cbBTC and USDC across multiple maturity dates. It is offer-driven: lenders and borrowers propose their own rates, maturities and terms rather than relying on a protocol-defined utilisation curve, and it externalises loan risk, rate and duration to market participants rather than replacing Blue ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/347128040805697)).

Faq.question: Who owns Morpho and where does value accrue?
Faq.answer: The Morpho Association, a shareholder-free French nonprofit, owns Morpho Labs SAS as a wholly owned subsidiary, so the MORPHO token is the only asset ([Morpho docs](https://docs.morpho.org/learn/governance/organization/), [DL News](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/morpho-nonprofit-to-absorb-development-team/)). The June 2026 $175M raise was structured as a token purchase agreement with proceeds to the Association at roughly a $2B valuation ([Lex Substack](https://lex.substack.com/p/defi-the-175mm-bet-on-morpho)).

bull.claim: Scale has compounded fast: Morpho Blue holds $7.516B TVL with $4.077B borrowed across 40-plus chains as of 26 July 2026, second only to Aave in this set (DefiLlama).

The capital and investor base is the strongest in the sector: $175M in June 2026 co-led by Paradigm, a16z crypto and Ribbit, with Apollo Funds, Circle Ventures and VanEck participating at roughly a $2B valuation (Lex Substack).

Enterprise distribution is proven: Morpho was the first protocol integrated directly by a major enterprise, with Coinbase issuing over $300M in bitcoin-backed loans through it, alongside Trust Wallet, Binance Wallet, Safe and Ledger (Morpho blog).

Immutability removes governance risk from live markets: parameters persist in perpetuity, market creation needs no vote, and governance's only economic lever is a fee switch capped at 25% of borrower interest (Morpho docs, Morpho docs).

bear.claim: Isolation does not prevent losses, it only localises them: the November 2025 Stream Finance collapse left roughly 3.6% bad debt in the MEV Capital vault and mapped roughly $285M of potential exposure across DeFi (Binance Square, The Block).
The credit event repeated within nine months: a Resolv exploit hit Morpho vaults in July 2026 and MORPHO fell 4.6% (CoinMarketCap).

Depositors are exposed to curator quality with no protocol backstop, which Morpho's own documentation acknowledges by publishing curator security considerations and a bad-debt handling tutorial (Morpho docs, Morpho docs).
Third-party risk scoring is mid-grade, not top-tier: Hindenrank assigned Morpho a B- grade at $7.1B TVL in its 2 May 2026 report (Hindenrank).

radiant.LongDescription: Radiant Capital was an omnichain money market: users deposited on one chain and borrowed against that collateral with withdrawals routed to other chains, initially through Stargate's stable router while collateral remained on Arbitrum ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/radiantv1/radiant-v1)). It was built on Aave contracts, evident in its GitHub organisation which forks `bgd-labs/aave-helpers` and `aave/aave-utilities` ([GitHub](https://github.com/radiant-capital)). The economic model paid 50% of platform fees to lenders and 50% to RDNT lockers, with RDNT rewards vesting linearly over 28 days and a 50% early-exit penalty redistributed to lockers ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/radiantv1/radiant-v1)). That model is now irrelevant: after the 16 October 2024 exploit the DAO began a formal wind-down on 1 June 2026, disabling lending across all Core and RIZv1 markets and ceasing RDNT emissions ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/329817870913330)). What remains is a withdrawal-and-remediation shell.

Faq.question: What exactly happened in the October 2024 exploit?
Faq.answer: On 16 October 2024 attackers compromised the devices of at least three Radiant developers through sophisticated malware injection. The Safe{Wallet} front-end displayed legitimate transaction data while malicious `transferOwnership` transactions were signed in the background; error messages prompted re-signing, yielding three valid malicious signatures. Tenderly simulations and manual review both returned normal, and Radiant described the compromise as completely undetectable ([Radiant post mortem](https://medium.com/@RadiantCapital/radiant-post-mortem-fecd6cd38081)). The loss is reported at roughly $50M by Radiant and crypto.news, $53M by Mandiant-linked coverage and $51M by a security researcher cited in The Block ([Crypto.news](https://crypto.news/radiant-capital-to-wind-down-after-50-million-north-korea-linked-hack/), [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/403254/unable-to-recover-from-roughly-50-million-hack-radiant-capital-is-winding-down)).

Faq.question: Who was responsible?
Faq.answer: Mandiant attributed the attack to UNC4736, also tracked as AppleJeus or Citrine Sleet, and assessed with high confidence that it has a DPRK nexus aligned with the Reconnaissance General Bureau. The initial access vector was an INLETDRIFT macOS backdoor delivered five weeks earlier via a Telegram message impersonating a former Radiant contractor ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

Faq.question: Why did a 3-of-11 multisig fail?
Faq.answer: Because the threshold was three and the attacker compromised three signer devices. The admin multisigs were 3-of-9 on Ethereum and Base and 3-of-11 on BSC and Arbitrum ([Radiant post mortem](https://medium.com/@RadiantCapital/radiant-post-mortem-fecd6cd38081)); The Defiant makes the point directly that the 3-of-11 configuration meant only three compromised devices were needed ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

Faq.question: Is Radiant still operating?
Faq.answer: No. The DAO wind-down began 1 June 2026. Lending is disabled across all Core and RIZv1 markets, RDNT emissions have ceased and treasury usage is restricted to essential matters. Users can still withdraw, repay, close positions, claim rewards and unlock dLP tokens; contracts remain immutable and accessible, the website runs until end of 2026 and the remediation portal remains available indefinitely ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/329817870913330)). The Block reported the DAO's own conclusion that there was no viable path forward and that it moves to a maintenance state ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/403254/unable-to-recover-from-roughly-50-million-hack-radiant-capital-is-winding-down)).

Faq.question: Will affected lenders be made whole?
Faq.answer: Not reliably. Eligible lending-market deposit losses are to be remediated 1:1 in kind, but only subject to available funds from protocol fees, future investments and partner contributions, and the plan explicitly does not guarantee full remediation, remaining subject to governance votes, treasury constraints and technical feasibility ([Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/remediation/remediation-plan)). Unlimited-allowance wallet drains are not eligible after a separate proposal failed quorum. With TVL at $613,179 on 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/radiant-v2)) and roughly $10.8M already laundered through Tornado Cash ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)), the recovery pool is minimal.

Faq.question: What was the roadmap before the wind-down?
Faq.answer: A February 2026 roadmap had committed to core blue-chip lending on upgraded Aave contracts plus isolated markets on Morpho, retiring the legacy RIZv1 stack. Recovery efforts included RFP-47, a merged-claim-contract approach, the Radiant Guardian Fund under RFP-52 and phased remediation for Convenience claimants, with payouts targeted for Q3 and Q4 2025 that then slipped ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist), [Radiant docs](https://docs.radiant.capital/radiant/remediation/remediation-plan)).

Faq.question: Is there any residual value in RDNT?
Faq.answer: Effectively no. At the wind-down announcement RDNT traded around $0.0015 with a $1.96M market cap and a rank of #2356, and Binance, OKX and Crypto.com had all delisted it by June 2026 ([The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/radiant-capital-winds-down-2m-husk-dprk-50m-heist)).

bull.claim: Contracts remain immutable and accessible and the remediation portal is available indefinitely, so users retain the ability to withdraw, repay, close positions, claim rewards and unlock dLP tokens (Binance Square).

The wind-down is orderly and governance-ratified rather than abandoned: a community council administers the plan, zeroShadow remains engaged within available resources and any recovered funds pass to affected investors (Binance Square, Radiant docs).

The Convenience Class actually delivered for the large majority of claimants: $10 to $1,000 claims at a 30% haircut covering 95% (28K) of affected users, distribution beginning Q4 2025 (Radiant docs).

The post mortem is unusually candid and technically detailed, naming compromised addresses, devices and multisig thresholds, which makes it a usable operational-security reference for other protocols (Radiant post mortem).

bear.claim: The protocol is dead as a going concern: lending disabled everywhere since 1 June 2026, emissions ceased, the DAO in a maintenance state with no viable path forward (Binance Square, The Block).
Capital destruction was near-total: $386.8M peak TVL in December 2023 down to $613,179 on 26 July 2026 (Crypto.news, DefiLlama).
Recovery is essentially off the table: CertiK observed 2,834 ETH, roughly $10.8M, moved through Tornado Cash by October 2025, and the attacker is a DPRK-nexus group (The Defiant).
Remediation is explicitly unguaranteed and one claim class was excluded entirely: unlimited-allowance wallet drains are not eligible after a proposal failed quorum (Radiant docs).

spark.LongDescription: Spark is the lending and capital-allocation arm of the Sky ecosystem, formerly MakerDAO, and describes itself as a two-sided capital allocator that borrows from Sky's stablecoin reserves and deploys capital across DeFi, CeFi and RWAs ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/faq)). It has three products: Spark Savings (vaults including sUSDS), SparkLend (a USDS-centric money market), and the Spark Liquidity Layer, which provides liquidity directly into DeFi markets across networks ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/faq)). SparkLend is a fork of the Aave V3 codebase, run conservatively with a narrow collateral set, multi-oracle pricing, strict rate limits and first-loss capital ([Contango](https://medium.com/contango-xyz/contango-x-spark-3c92a9c746fc), [Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). Rates are hybrid: a variable rate driven by supply and demand within SparkLend, plus transparent rates that behave as a short-term fixed rate and change only through Sky Governance ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). Liquidation is Aave-style: below a health factor of 1 but above 0.95, up to 50% of debt can be covered; at or below 0.95, up to 100% ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)).

OffchainFacts.value: Spark Protocol and SparkLend launched 9 May 2023 as part of MakerDAO's Endgame era; first deployed on mainnet in March 2023 and officially launched in May after initial MakerDAO funding

Spark Foundation is the GitHub organisation owner; Phoenix Labs is the R&D company that built and contributes to Spark, and is a whitelisted "nested contributor" that can submit governance proposals

spark.OrgIntro:
Where Spark's mandate ends and Sky's begins. This distinction matters more for Spark than for any other entity in the set, so it is set out explicitly.

- Sky owns the balance sheet. Spark borrows from Sky's stablecoin reserves and is described as the distribution layer within the SKY ecosystem, with SKY as the parent protocol; the Spark treasury acts as junior capital required by SKY to fulfil the risk-required capital needs for accessing the SKY credit line ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/faq), [Spark Q1 2026 report](https://paragraph.com/@spark-11/spark-q1-2026-financial-report)).
- Sky Governance sets SparkLend's risk parameters. Per-market supply and borrow caps are configured by Sky Governance, transparent rates change based on Sky Governance, and Sky Governance can reduce borrowing power of any asset to 0% without impacting existing borrowers ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)).
- Sky controls SPK supply and distribution. 65% of the 10 billion genesis supply sits with Sky for a 10-year farming campaign following rules set in the Sky Atlas, and Sky retains the ability to mint additional SPK under extreme circumstances ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/governance/spk-token)).
- Spark governs itself through Atlas edits, not independent sovereignty. The Spark governance process centres on updating the Spark Agent artifact in the Sky Atlas, which controls budgets, risk settings, asset onboarding, SLL integrations and new chain deployments; proposals are filed in the Spark Prime section of the Sky forum and voted on Snapshot with SPK ([Spark governance docs](https://docs.spark.fi/governance)).
- Historically the ownership was even more direct. All products created by Phoenix Labs were to belong to MakerDAO, inheriting Maker's governance system, and Phoenix Labs committed 10% of DAI-market profits to Aave DAO for the first two years as a fork licence ([Binance Square](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/213372), [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2023/02/08/makerdao-contributors-propose-first-native-liquidity-market-focused-on-dai-stablecoin)).

Faq.question: Has SparkLend ever taken bad debt?
Faq.answer: No bad-debt event appears in the fetched sources, and the closest live test went the other way. When Kelp DAO's bridge was compromised on 18 April 2026 and 116,500 unbacked rsETH were minted, Aave V3 and V4 faced roughly $195M of potential bad debt while SparkLend was left with $37,300 of frozen residual rsETH, worth 15.32 rsETH, because PhoenixLabs had filed an exit proposal on 16 January 2026 and halted new rsETH supply by spell on 29 January 2026 ([KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/sparklend-exits-rseth-on-same-day-aave-expands-exposure)). Spark's own framing is that its risk pillars are designed to stack so that a failure in any single component, oracle, issuer, liquidator or market liquidity, does not cascade into bad debt ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). Spark co-founder Sam MacPherson nonetheless cautioned on 19 April 2026 that protocols claiming no rsETH exposure may still carry indirect exposure through user collateral ([KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/sparklend-exits-rseth-on-same-day-aave-expands-exposure)).

Faq.question: Who sets the interest rates?
Faq.answer: Not the utilisation curve alone. SparkLend rates respond to supply and demand, but transparent rates act as a fixed rate in the short term and change based on Sky Governance, and the Spark Liquidity Layer automatically moves USDS, USDC and USDT into and out of SparkLend based on target borrow rates, utilisation and available inventory at other venues ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). In practice Sky Governance sets the target and the SLL enforces it by supplying or withdrawing inventory, which is closer to a central-bank standing facility than to a pure market-clearing curve. Per-market supply and borrow caps are also configured by Sky Governance ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)).

Faq.question: What happens at liquidation?
Faq.answer: If a position's health factor drops below 1 but stays above 0.95, up to 50% of the position's debt can be covered in a liquidation call; at or below 0.95, up to 100% can be covered, with the collateral transferred depending on debt covered, oracle prices and the applicable liquidation bonus ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). Governance has a softer tool as well: the borrowing power of any asset can be reduced to 0% without impacting existing borrowers, which lets it phase out a collateral type without forcing liquidations as the first response ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)). Forced liquidation is still used when required, as with the remaining BTC e-mode positions on 8 June 2026 ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/sparklend)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: Spark and Sky publish an explicit six-layer loss waterfall: internal junior risk capital at the Prime level, then Prime-external junior risk capital, then external senior risk capital via srUSDS (planned, not yet deployed), then the Sky Surplus Buffer, then Sky's Aggregate Surplus Buffer, then a SKY token backstop where Sky mints SKY to recapitalise ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/spark-savings)). Only if all of that is exhausted are residual losses socialised equally across all USDS holders, including Spark Savings vaults ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/spark-savings)). Spark holds over $35M of stablecoin equity capital at Layer 1 and describes the aggregate protection as several hundred million dollars ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/spark-savings)). Credora's model puts the Probability of Significant Loss at 0.39% for the ETH vault and 0.46% to 0.52% for the stablecoin vaults, rising to 1.03% for stUSDS, as of 29 June 2026 ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/products/spark-savings/risk-architecture/credora-rating)).

Faq.question: How independent is Spark from Sky?
Faq.answer: Materially less than the separate brand suggests. Spark borrows from Sky's stablecoin reserves and operates as a two-sided capital allocator deploying that capital across DeFi, CeFi and RWAs ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/faq)), and its Q1 2026 report calls SKY the parent protocol and describes the Spark treasury as junior capital required by SKY to access the SKY credit line ([Spark Q1 2026 report](https://paragraph.com/@spark-11/spark-q1-2026-financial-report)). Spark's own governance process is a process for amending the Spark Agent artifact inside the Sky Atlas, filed in the Spark Prime section of the Sky forum and voted on Snapshot at s:sparkfi.eth, with a Spark Risk Council review that can reject a proposal before it reaches a vote ([Spark governance docs](https://docs.spark.fi/governance)). Hindenrank scores this dependency as the number one risk, noting that solvency is backstopped by Sky's $6.5B reserve and that this creates single-entity systemic risk ([Hindenrank](https://hindenrank.com/protocol/spark)).

Faq.question: Where does Spark actually make its money?
Faq.answer: Mostly from the Spark Liquidity Layer, not from SparkLend. In Q1 2026 the SLL ran $1.93B of average deployment at a 5.8% average APY for $27.62M of gross returns and $3.05M net, on a captured spread of 0.64%, while SparkLend contributed only $156k of revenue, down from $215k in Q4 ([Spark Q1 2026 report](https://paragraph.com/@spark-11/spark-q1-2026-financial-report)). Distribution rewards added $3.31M, led by sUSDS at $1.66M and stUSDS at $710k ([Spark Q1 2026 report](https://paragraph.com/@spark-11/spark-q1-2026-financial-report)). A credit analyst should therefore treat Spark primarily as a leveraged stablecoin carry book with a money market attached, not as a lending protocol whose earnings scale with borrow demand.

Faq.question: What does the SPK token actually control, and what is the supply risk?
Faq.answer: SPK is used for signalling and Snapshot voting on the Spark Agent artifact, with eligible proposers being holders of 1% of supply, 100M SPK, or nested contributors such as Phoenix Labs ([Spark governance docs](https://docs.spark.fi/governance)). Of the 10 billion genesis supply, 65% sits with Sky for a 10-year farming campaign emitting 1,625M per year in years one and two and tapering to 203.13M per year by year seven, 23% is ecosystem and 12% is team on a 12-month 25% cliff then three-year vest, and Sky retains the ability to mint additional SPK under extreme circumstances per the Sky Atlas ([Spark docs](https://docs.spark.fi/governance/spk-token)). The 17 June 2026 unlock alone was 769,050,000 SPK, about 24.1% of market capitalisation, following a 17 May 2026 unlock that preceded a 25.6% price decline within 12 days ([Crypto Daily](https://cryptodaily.co.uk/2026/06/spark-spk-unlock-yield-infrastructure)).

bull.claim: Spark is profitable through a weak lending quarter: Q1 2026 gross protocol returns of $31.5M, net protocol returns of $6.91M, a net protocol surplus of $3.46M, a treasury up 5.7% quarter on quarter to $46.1M, and the first $986k of SPK buybacks initiated (Spark Q1 2026 report).

The conservative listing policy has already paid out once: in the April 2026 Kelp rsETH incident Aave V3 and V4 faced roughly $195M of potential bad debt while SparkLend was left holding $37,300 of frozen residual rsETH, having exited the asset by spell on 29 January 2026 (KuCoin).

The loss buffer is unusually deep and independently rated: six explicit loss-absorption layers up to a SKY token backstop, over $35M of Prime-level stablecoin equity capital and several hundred million dollars of aggregate protection (Spark docs), with Credora putting stablecoin vault Probability of Significant Loss at 0.46% to 0.52% and the ETH vault at 0.39% as of 29 June 2026 (Spark docs).

Scale and institutional distribution are real: $4.63B of TVL across Spark and $3.72B in SparkLend as of 26 July 2026 (DefiLlama, DefiLlama), $4.5B of distributed supply, $285M of SparkLend USDT balances making it one of the largest USDT lending venues on Ethereum, and Spark Institutional Lending at $150M deployed against a governance-approved $1B ceiling through an Anchorage tri-party structure (Spark Q1 2026 report).

bear.claim: Spark is not an independent credit: Hindenrank grades it B- with a risk score of 28/100 and names deep dependency on the Sky ecosystem as risk number one, since solvency is backstopped by Sky's $6.5B reserve and that concentrates systemic risk in a single entity (Hindenrank). S&P's first-ever stablecoin-system credit rating put Sky Protocol, the parent, at B- with a stable outlook (Steakhouse Financial).

The core lending business is shrinking, not growing: SparkLend Q1 2026 revenue of $156k was down from $215k in Q4, and the SLL's captured spread compressed from 0.83% in January to 0.41% in March against 0.70% in Q4 (Spark Q1 2026 report). Spark also initiated a wind-down of the SparkLend Gnosis Chain instance in the quarter (Spark Q1 2026 report).

Collateral concentration was loosened materially at exactly the wrong scale: Hindenrank flags the May 2026 governance decision to raise the WBTC supply cap tenfold from 3,000 to 30,000 BTC, concentrating up to roughly $2.85B of potential BTC collateral exposure, and warns that a severe BTC drawdown could trigger correlated liquidations exceeding SparkLend's isolated-pool buffers (Hindenrank).

Token supply is a persistent overhang and governance is nascent: 65% of the 10 billion SPK supply is still being emitted by Sky over ten years and Sky can mint more under extreme circumstances (Spark docs), the 17 June 2026 unlock alone was worth about 24.1% of market capitalisation (Crypto Daily), and Hindenrank flags governance capture risk during the early low-participation phase (Hindenrank).

gearbox.LongDescription: Gearbox is a two sided credit protocol: passive lenders deposit into ERC-4626 pools, and active users open Credit Accounts, isolated smart contract wallets that hold both the user collateral and the borrowed funds and can only call whitelisted adapters and hold whitelisted tokens ([Gearbox dev docs, V2 architecture overview](https://github.com/Gearbox-protocol/dev-docs/blob/main/pages/v2/architecture/overview.md)). Because the borrowed capital never leaves the account, Gearbox can extend leverage well above what a normal overcollateralised loan allows while still enforcing a health factor check after every single call ([Gearbox dev docs](https://github.com/Gearbox-protocol/dev-docs/blob/main/pages/v2/architecture/overview.md)). The original design was published as a tech paper in April 2021 by Mikhail Lazarev and Ilgiz Gimaltdinov, framing Credit Accounts as a new DeFi primitive for margin trading, leveraged farming and leveraged CDPs ([Gearbox tech paper](https://static.gearbox.finance/docs/Gearbox.pdf)). V3 added quotas and gauges, so GEAR stakers vote on the extra rate borrowers pay per collateral asset, and moved the protocol toward a permissionless, curator operated market model where the DAO builds rails and Market Curators set risk parameters ([Gearbox docs, Protocol DAO](https://docs.gearbox.finance/about-gearbox/governance-and-operations/protocol-dao)). Current documentation frames Credit Accounts as user owned smart contract wallets with solvency checks behind every action, targeted at both retail and institutional flows ([Gearbox docs, Powered by Credit Accounts](https://docs.gearbox.finance/introduction/powered-by-credit-accounts)).

Faq.question: Where does bad debt land if a Credit Account goes underwater?
Faq.answer: Liquidation is meant to close the account before equity is exhausted. If a shortfall still occurs, the protocol first absorbs it from unclaimed protocol fees, and any remainder is socialised across pool depositors through a reduction in the Diesel (LP) token exchange rate ([Gearbox liquidation dynamics](https://docs.gearbox.finance/core/liquidation-dynamics)). Passive lenders are therefore the residual bearer of loss, not the DAO treasury.

Faq.question: Who sets the interest rate a lender earns?
Faq.answer: Base rates come from a two kink utilisation curve configured per pool with parameters U1, U2, base rate and three slopes ([Gearbox markets and rates](https://docs.gearbox.finance/developers/gm-markets-rates)). On top of that, quota rates are set either by GEAR stakers voting in gauges or by a market curator, and that extra fee is split between passive lenders and the DAO ([GEAR utility and staking](https://docs.gearbox.finance/gear-token/utility-and-staking)).

Faq.question: How does liquidation actually work?
Faq.answer: Health factor is total weighted value divided by total debt, checked after every call a Credit Account makes; falling below the threshold allows liquidation, which can be partial or full ([Gearbox dev docs](https://github.com/Gearbox-protocol/dev-docs/blob/main/pages/v2/architecture/overview.md), [Gearbox liquidation dynamics](https://docs.gearbox.finance/core/liquidation-dynamics)). Liquidators take a premium of roughly 3% to 4% and the protocol takes 1% to 1.5% ([Gearbox protocol fees](https://docs.gearbox.finance/overview/protocol-fees)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a passive lender?
Faq.answer: The worst case is a correlated collateral shock or an oracle failure that leaves accounts insolvent faster than liquidators can act, at which point losses hit the Diesel exchange rate directly ([Gearbox liquidation dynamics](https://docs.gearbox.finance/core/liquidation-dynamics)). The historical average leverage across Credit Accounts has been high, around 5.57x with a weighted average health factor of 1.105 in one 2023 monthly report, which is a thin buffer ([Gearbox April protocol update](https://medium.com/gearbox-protocol/gearbox-april-protocol-update-9c4d309d5b2f)).

Faq.question: Can the DAO seize or reprice a live market?
Faq.answer: No. Documentation states explicitly that the DAO cannot change risk parameters of a live curator managed market and cannot seize or reallocate deposits; it governs versions, chain activation and the fee split ([Gearbox docs, Protocol DAO](https://docs.gearbox.finance/about-gearbox/governance-and-operations/protocol-dao)). That is a credit positive for market isolation and a credit negative for the DAO's ability to intervene in a crisis.

Faq.question: Has Gearbox ever had a loss event?
Faq.answer: Public claims of zero security incidents and zero bad debt over five years come from the co-founder in a July 2026 conference talk, not from an independent audit of the record ([Mikhail Lazarev talk summary](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HcD37L1mVxI)). Treat it as a management assertion. No third party incident post mortem for Gearbox was found in this session.

Faq.question: How fast can the protocol respond to an emergency?
Faq.answer: A 4 of 12 veto and unpause multisig exists for rapid response, deliberately limited so it can only block, never propose ([V3.0 operational multisigs](https://docs.gearbox.finance/about-gearbox/governance-and-operations/v3.0-operational-multisigs)). Technical changes otherwise sit behind a 2 day timelock ([V3.0 operational multisigs](https://docs.gearbox.finance/about-gearbox/governance-and-operations/v3.0-operational-multisigs)).

bull.claim: Credit Accounts monetise better than plain money markets: Messari estimated return on assets nearly seven times higher than traditional lending protocols and modelled 70% TVL growth to roughly $230m (Messari, Lending Renaissance, 12 March 2024).
Governance and execution are genuinely separated: any user can execute a queued, non vetoed transaction after timelock, removing multisig dependency (Updated governance flow).

The permissionless curator model lets third parties launch markets without a DAO vote while the DAO keeps the bytecode registry, which scales the protocol without scaling governance load (Gearbox docs, Protocol DAO).
Deep audit coverage across V2 and V3 from ChainSecurity, ABDK, Consensys Diligence and Decurity, plus a live Immunefi program with $427.4k paid to date (Gearbox audits, Immunefi Gearbox).

bear.claim: TVL of $18.42m on 26 July 2026 is about 4.4% of the April 2024 peak of $419.3m, so the lender base that funds the whole model has largely left (DefiLlama API, gearbox).
Total capital raised is only about $8.04m across three rounds, which is thin funding for a protocol maintaining eleven chain deployments (DefiLlama Gearbox, DefiLlama API, gearbox).
Historic average leverage of roughly 5.57x with a weighted average health factor of 1.105 leaves very little room before liquidation across the book (Gearbox April protocol update).

Governance discussion has partly migrated off the public forum into Discord, with forum sections labelled as moved, which reduces the auditable public record a credit analyst can rely on (gov.gearbox.fi).

Instead of charging interest, Stella uses a Pay As You Earn model: borrowers, called leveragoors, pay nothing while a position is open, and Stella takes a cut of the net profit only when a profitable position is closed ([Stella strategy docs](https://docs.stellaxyz.io/stella-doc/protocol-mechanism/stella-strategy)). Of that yield cut, 20% is collected as protocol fees accruing to ALPHA stakers ([Stella FAQ](https://docs.stellaxyz.io/stella-doc/additional-information/faq)). The lineage carries a heavy credit history: a February 2021 exploit of roughly $37.5m drawn from Cream's Iron Bank, and a bad debt dispute that ran into 2023 ([Cream Finance post mortem](https://medium.com/cream-finance/alpha-homora-v2-exploit-post-mortem-344d277bdea6), [DL News, 2023](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/defi-partners-clash-over-32m-bad-debt-iron-bank-alpha-homora/)).

Faq.question: Is Stella still operating?
Faq.answer: No wind down notice was found, and the docs remain live, but DefiLlama shows TVL flat near $443k with a final datapoint of 10 June 2026 and zero incentives ([DefiLlama API, stella](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/stella)). The Alpha Venture DAO blog's most recent visible material dates to the May 2023 Iron Bank dispute ([Alpha Venture DAO blog](https://blog.alphaventuredao.io/)). Treat the protocol as functionally dormant with residual deposits.

Faq.question: Where did the bad debt from the 2021 exploit end up?
Faq.answer: It ended up on Cream's Iron Bank balance sheet, since the exploiter borrowed through Alpha Homora's privileged access rather than draining Alpha's own reserves ([Origin Protocol incident note](https://github.com/OriginProtocol/security/blob/master/incidents/2021-02-13-Alpha-Homora-v2.md)). Iron Bank paused Alpha Homora's lending accounts in March 2023 over roughly $32m still outstanding, and the two sides disputed the repayment terms publicly ([DL News](https://www.dlnews.com/articles/defi/defi-partners-clash-over-32m-bad-debt-iron-bank-alpha-homora/)).

Faq.question: How is the lender compensated if there is no borrow interest?
Faq.answer: Through a share of realised profit. Stella takes a cut of the net yield when a profitable position closes, and 20% of that cut becomes protocol fees accruing to ALPHA stakers ([Stella FAQ](https://docs.stellaxyz.io/stella-doc/additional-information/faq)). If borrowers close flat or at a loss, the lender's realised return from that position is zero.

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender here?
Faq.answer: Two overlapping risks. First, the 2021 precedent: a protocol level exploit that converts lender capital into a multi year negotiated claim rather than an immediate loss ([Iron Bank timeline](https://ibdotxyz.medium.com/timeline-between-iron-bank-alpha-homora-v2-e0bfe75467b8)). Second, the academic finding that in Alpha Homora 72.35% of leverage taking borrowers had a negative APY once governance token incentives are stripped out, which implies weak organic demand for the borrow side that funds lender returns ([Wang et al., Speculative Multipliers on DeFi](https://fc22.ifca.ai/preproceedings/71.pdf)).

Faq.question: Is governance live?
Faq.answer: Not as documented. Kraken's asset statement records that ALPHA stakers were to receive sALPHA for governance, which was "not live yet at the time of writing" ([Kraken UK crypto asset statement, Stella](https://assets-cms.kraken.com/files/51n36hrp/facade/400112dfaed7a751d09ea875c21aae46fdb699b9.pdf)). No Snapshot space or on chain governor for Stella was located in this session.

Faq.question: How were liquidations handled historically?
Faq.answer: Alpha Homora liquidated leveraged AMM positions when the collateral ratio breached the threshold, and the empirical record shows 270 of 10,430 analysed positions were liquidated over a nine month window, with the largest single liquidation loss at 10.63% of collateral ([Wang et al., Speculative Multipliers on DeFi](https://fc22.ifca.ai/preproceedings/71.pdf)). Arbitrage loss was a bigger tail risk in some cases, with one position losing 81.67% of collateral ([Wang et al.](https://fc22.ifca.ai/preproceedings/71.pdf)).

Faq.question: Does the ALPHA token have a claim on anything today?
Faq.answer: Documented claim is a fee stream from Stella activity, but with TVL under half a million dollars that stream is negligible ([Stella FAQ](https://docs.stellaxyz.io/stella-doc/additional-information/faq), [DefiLlama API, stella](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/stella)). Total supply is 1 billion with 15% to team and advisors and 36.67% to ecosystem ([Stella token distribution](https://docs.stellaxyz.io/stella-doc/tokenomics/token-distribution)).

bull.claim: The 0% borrow cost Pay As You Earn model is genuinely differentiated: borrowers pay only out of realised profit, with 20% of the yield cut becoming protocol fees (Stella FAQ).
The founding team remained intact through the rebrand, with Tascha, Nipun and Arin all confirmed in place (Stella FAQ).
The protocol survived a $37m exploit and relaunched to $675m TVL within three months in 2021, which is a demonstrated recovery capability (Cointelegraph).
Post exploit controls were specific and verifiable: EOA-only execute, whitelisted spells, governor-only resolveReserve (Alpha Venture DAO recap).

bear.claim: TVL of $442,829 with the data series ending 10 June 2026 and zero incentives in every window is consistent with a dormant protocol (DefiLlama API, stella).
The credit record includes a roughly $37m exploit and a roughly $32m bad debt that a counterparty lender had to pause accounts over two years later (Cream Finance post mortem, DL News).

Peer reviewed analysis of the predecessor product found 72.35% of leveraged borrowers earned a negative APY absent token incentives, undermining the economic case for the borrow side (Wang et al., Speculative Multipliers on DeFi).

extra-finance.LongDescription: Extra Finance is a leveraged yield farming protocol built for the Superchain, originally on Optimism and now with most of its capital on Base ([Extra Finance docs](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance), [DefiLlama API, extra-finance](https://api.llama.fi/protocol/extra-finance)). Lenders supply single assets into lending pools; farmers borrow from those pools to open leveraged LP positions in supported DEX pairs at up to 3x and higher depending on the pool ([Extra Finance docs](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance)). The protocol has since added XLend, an Aave V3 fork wrapped in smart accounts that gives users multiple isolated sub accounts, bundled transactions and gas free operations ([ExtraFi XLend docs](https://docs.extrafi.io/extrafi-xlend), [XLend audits page](https://docs.extrafi.io/extrafi-xlend/security/audits-and-security)). Value accrues to veEXTRA holders: protocol fees are used to buy back EXTRA which is distributed to lockers each epoch ([EXTRA tokenomics part II](https://medium.com/@ExtraFinance/extra-tokenomics-part-%E2%85%B1-emission-plan-55ca6a9f874f)). The team is pseudonymous and the codebase is only partially open sourced ([Extra Finance FAQ](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance/faq)).

Faq.question: Who bears bad debt if a leveraged farm position goes underwater?
Faq.answer: The lending pool depositors. Extra Finance's leveraged yield farming design borrows from single asset lending pools to build the LP position, so any shortfall after liquidation falls on the pool ([Introduction to leveraged yield farming](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance/leverage-farming/introduction-to-leveraged-yield-farming)). No public loss event was found in this session, and no insurance fund or backstop is documented.

Faq.question: How are lending rates set?
Faq.answer: Extra Finance uses a pseudo fixed interest rate model on its lending pools rather than a purely floating utilisation curve ([Extra Finance docs](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance)). XLend, being an Aave V3 fork, inherits Aave's rate architecture ([XLend audits page](https://docs.extrafi.io/extrafi-xlend/security/audits-and-security)).

Faq.question: How much leverage is available?
Faq.answer: The official documentation describes up to 3x and higher depending on the pool ([Extra Finance docs](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance)). Third party writeups have described up to 7x for veEXTRA holders in select pools, so the effective ceiling depends on the pool and the user's lock ([Vesper Finance deep dive](https://medium.com/vesperfinance/extra-finance-deep-dive-9413d2b8f505)). A credit analyst should treat the pool level parameter, not the headline, as the binding constraint.

Faq.question: Is the protocol profitable, and does that flow to token holders?
Faq.answer: DefiLlama shows the leveraged farming sub-protocol with $8.19m cumulative fees and revenue running at roughly $51,415 in Q3 2025, down from $919,432 in Q4 2024, with token holder net income appearing only from Q2 2025 onward ([DefiLlama, Extra Finance leverage farming earnings](https://defillama.com/protocol/extra-finance-leverage-farming?tvl=false&events=false&earnings=true)). Fees are used to buy back EXTRA distributed to veEXTRA lockers each epoch ([EXTRA tokenomics part II](https://medium.com/@ExtraFinance/extra-tokenomics-part-%E2%85%B1-emission-plan-55ca6a9f874f)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: A fast correlated move in a leveraged LP pair on a chain with thin liquidation liquidity, leaving the lending pool with unrecoverable debt. The structural aggravator is that the team is pseudonymous with no named legal entity, so there is no off chain counterparty to pursue ([Extra Finance FAQ](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance/faq)). There is also no bug bounty program to catch vulnerabilities before they are exploited ([Extra Finance audits and security](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance/audits-and-security)).

Faq.question: How centralised is governance in practice?
Faq.answer: Proposals require 30,000 veEXTRA and a 50,000 veEXTRA quorum, with discussion in a Discord channel before Snapshot submission ([ve-mechanism and utility V2](https://docs.extrafi.io/extra_finance/tokenomics/ve-mechanism-and-utility-v2), [Extra Finance docs governance summary](https://docingest.com/docs/docs.extrafi.io)). Voting power is measured on Optimism mainnet balances, which concentrates governance on the smaller of its two main chains ([Extra Finance docs governance summary](https://docingest.com/docs/docs.extrafi.io)).

Faq.question: What third party risk oversight exists?
Faq.answer: Gauntlet curates the ExtraFi XLend WETH Vault on Morpho on Base, which crossed $20M in deposits in August 2025 ([ExtraFi on X](https://x.com/ExtraFi_io/status/1956322565443449311)). That is curator oversight of a vault that routes into ExtraFi, not a risk mandate over the core protocol.

bull.claim: Three independent audits from BlockSec, PeckShield and Sherlock, with the XLend money market being an Aave V3 fork that inherits Aave's audit surface (Extra Finance audits and security, XLend audits page).
Ranked first by the Optimism Grants Council among 23 protocols in the Season 7 grants ranking, unlocking a 100,000 OP grant (Optimism Collective).
Real cumulative revenue: $8.19m of cumulative fees on the leveraged farming product alone, with a documented buyback to veEXTRA lockers (DefiLlama earnings view, EXTRA tokenomics part II).
Product diversification is working directionally: XLend went from $135.49K at launch in February 2025 to over $3M by April 2025 (Extra Finance monthly review, February 2025, April 2025).

bear.claim: TVL of $27.04m on 26 July 2026 is roughly 15% of the December 2024 peak of $177.39m (DefiLlama API, extra-finance).
Revenue has collapsed alongside it: $51,415 in Q3 2025 against $919,432 in Q4 2024, a fall of roughly 94% (DefiLlama earnings view).
Fully pseudonymous team, no disclosed legal entity or jurisdiction, and code that is only partially open sourced (Extra Finance FAQ).
No bug bounty program is documented anywhere in the security pages, which is a material gap for a protocol holding tens of millions in leveraged positions (Extra Finance audits and security).

fluid.LongDescription: Fluid is a unified liquidity protocol built by the Instadapp team, in which a single Liquidity Layer sits underneath a lending market, vaults and a native DEX, so the same dollar of deposits backs multiple functions at once ([Instadapp blog, Fluid introduction, 10 Oct 2023](https://blog.instadapp.io/fluid/)). Its two signature primitives are Smart Collateral, where collateral is simultaneously deployed as DEX liquidity earning trading fees, and Smart Debt, where the borrowed position itself acts as DEX liquidity so trading fees offset borrowing cost ([Instadapp blog, Fluid DEX, 19 Jun 2024](https://blog.instadapp.io/fluid-dex/)). The Liquidity Layer is deliberately minimal, a contract that stores assets and validates supply, borrow, repay and withdraw with automated per block debt and collateral ceilings, while rate logic and risk management live in modules on top ([OAK Research, Fluid](https://oakresearch.io/en/reports/protocols/fluid-new-defi-standard-unify-dex-lending)). That architecture supports LTVs up to 95% with liquidation penalties as low as 0.1% via a tick based liquidation engine where traders act as liquidators ([Instadapp blog, Fluid introduction](https://blog.instadapp.io/fluid/)). The Instadapp governance token INST was renamed FLUID at a 1:1 ratio in December 2024, keeping the same token address and 100M supply ([Rebranding and Growth Plan for Fluid Protocol](https://gov.fluid.io/t/rebranding-and-growth-plan-for-fluid-protocol/985)).

Faq.question: What exactly is the Instadapp relationship?
Faq.answer: Instadapp is the team and the original DeFi aggregator; Fluid is the protocol it built, and the INST governance token was renamed FLUID 1:1 in December 2024 with the same contract address and 100M supply ([Rebranding and Growth Plan](https://gov.fluid.io/t/rebranding-and-growth-plan-for-fluid-protocol/985)). The formal issuer named in the MiCA whitepaper is Interop Labs Ltd. of the BVI ([Instadapp MiCA whitepaper](https://instadapp.io/mica-whitepaper.pdf)). The bug bounty is still listed under the Instadapp program on Immunefi ([Immunefi Instadapp](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/instadapp/information/)).

Faq.question: What are Smart Collateral and Smart Debt, in credit terms?
Faq.answer: Smart Collateral means posted collateral simultaneously earns DEX trading fees; Smart Debt means the borrowed position itself provides DEX liquidity, so trading fees reduce net borrowing cost ([Instadapp blog, Fluid DEX](https://blog.instadapp.io/fluid-dex/)). For a lender this raises effective yield per unit of deposit, but it also means the same capital is exposed to lending risk and market making risk at the same time.

Faq.question: Where does bad debt land?
Faq.answer: The Liquidity Layer is shared, so a critical failure in the base contract would compromise Lending, Vaults and DEX simultaneously; this concentration is explicitly identified as the protocol's principal technical risk in a third party assessment ([Envelop audit report, April 2026](https://index.envelop.is/reports/fluid_audit.html)). The mitigating design is the automated per block ceiling system, which throttles abnormal withdrawals or risky loans and buys governance time to intervene ([OAK Research, Fluid](https://oakresearch.io/en/reports/protocols/fluid-new-defi-standard-unify-dex-lending)).

Faq.question: How does liquidation work at 95% LTV?
Faq.answer: Fluid uses a tick based liquidation engine in which traders act as liquidators, allowing penalties as low as 0.1% ([Instadapp blog, Fluid introduction](https://blog.instadapp.io/fluid/)). The tradeoff is that the buffer between a healthy and an insolvent position is very thin, so the system depends on liquidators being present and gas being available in exactly the market conditions where both are scarce.

Faq.question: Do FLUID holders receive protocol revenue?
Faq.answer: Not automatically. Blockworks' token transparency filing states token holders currently have no direct value accrual mechanism, and that any dividends, buybacks or fee distribution would require a governance vote ([Blockworks Token Transparency filing, Fluid](https://blockworks.com/token-transparency/filing/fluid)). The MiCA whitepaper records that a Q4 2025 buyback program was approved by governance ([Instadapp MiCA whitepaper](https://instadapp.io/mica-whitepaper.pdf)), and the December 2024 rebrand proposal set the trigger at $10m annualised revenue ([Rebranding and Growth Plan](https://gov.fluid.io/t/rebranding-and-growth-plan-for-fluid-protocol/985)).

Faq.question: What is the worst case for a lender?
Faq.answer: A critical bug in the shared Liquidity Layer, which functions as a single honeypot across all sub-protocols ([Envelop audit report](https://index.envelop.is/reports/fluid_audit.html)). The MiCA whitepaper is explicit that there is no insurance and no deposit guarantee ([Instadapp MiCA whitepaper](https://instadapp.io/mica-whitepaper.pdf)). A second, slower worst case is governance capture, given a 4M FLUID quorum against a 100M supply and a 1 day timelock ([Yearn Curation, Fluid Lending Protocol](https://curation.yearn.fi/report/fluid/)).

Faq.question: How fast can governance act in an emergency?
Faq.answer: Onchain GovernorBravo has a roughly 1 day voting delay, a roughly 2 day voting period and a 1 day timelock, so a full governance cycle is several days ([Yearn Curation, Fluid Lending Protocol](https://curation.yearn.fi/report/fluid/)). Faster protection comes from the automated ceilings, not from governance ([OAK Research, Fluid](https://oakresearch.io/en/reports/protocols/fluid-new-defi-standard-unify-dex-lending)).

bull.claim: Genuine capital efficiency: a Q1 2025 review recorded $18.3m of fees, up 62.6% quarter on quarter, with $2M of net earnings and no incentive program beyond 1.5M POL for the Polygon launch (Alea Research, Fluid).

Scale is real and institutionally validated: $796.5m TVL with $755.2m borrowed as of 26 July 2026, and the Aave DAO bought $4M of the token at a $350m FDV (DefiLlama API, fluid, Aave governance, ARFC Fluid alignment).

Strongest security posture of the four entities: four audit firms across Liquidity Layer, Vault and DEX, a $500,000 maximum Immunefi bounty and an additional $80,000 audit competition (Fluid audits and security, Immunefi Instadapp, Immunefi IOP Fluid Protocol).

Best disclosure of the four: a named BVI issuer, a published MiCA whitepaper, onchain-verified governance parameters and a third party token transparency filing (Instadapp MiCA whitepaper, Yearn Curation, Blockworks Token Transparency filing).

bear.claim: TVL has fallen from a peak of $2.684bn on 9 October 2025 to $796.5m, a decline of roughly 70% in under a year (DefiLlama API, fluid).

The shared Liquidity Layer is a single point of catastrophic failure across Lending, Vaults and DEX, and cumulative earnings are historically negative at about minus $192.3M due to past incentive distributions (Envelop audit report, April 2026).
Token concentration is high, with roughly 94% of supply in the top 100 wallets, against a governance quorum of only 4M FLUID out of 100M (Envelop audit report, Yearn Curation).
FLUID holders have no automatic claim on revenue; every value accrual mechanism requires a separate governance vote (Blockworks Token Transparency filing, Fluid).

pendle.LongDescription: Pendle splits any yield bearing token into a Principal Token (PT) and a Yield Token (YT) with a fixed maturity, so the fixed and floating legs of an onchain yield can be priced and traded separately ([Pendle docs, Introduction](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/Introduction)). A yield bearing asset is first wrapped into a Standardised Yield (SY) token, then SY is stripped into PT plus YT, and holding both is economically identical to holding the underlying ([Pendle Academy, yield tokenisation basics](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-academy/pendle-101/chapter-2-yield-tokenization-basics)). PT is described by Pendle itself as "essentially a zero-coupon bond on the underlying asset" that redeems 1:1 at maturity, while the PT holder forgoes the variable yield and points ([Pendle docs, PT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/PT)). YT streams the yield until expiry and then decays to zero, which gives leveraged exposure to a yield or points stream ([Pendle docs, YT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/YT)). Boros, launched in 2025, extends the same idea to perpetual funding rates, where a position "= user has to pay an interest stream and receive another interest stream until a maturity" ([Boros Litepaper](https://docs.pendle.finance/boros-dev/LitePaper)).

Faq.question: What exactly do I own when I buy a PT?
Faq.answer: A claim on one unit of the underlying yield bearing asset at maturity, bought at a discount today. Pendle's own documentation calls PT "essentially a zero-coupon bond on the underlying asset" and states that it can be redeemed 1:1 for the underlying after maturity, with the holder giving up the variable yield and any points in exchange for the fixed discount ([Pendle docs, PT](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/ProtocolMechanics/YieldTokenization/PT)).

Faq.question: Can a PT lose money if I hold to maturity?
Faq.answer: Not from rate movements, because it redeems 1:1 at maturity, but yes from the underlying asset. PT plus YT always equals the underlying, so any impairment of the yield bearing asset flows straight through to the PT ([Pendle Academy](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-academy/pendle-101/chapter-2-yield-tokenization-basics)).

Faq.question: Why did Pendle's TVL fall so far in 2026?
Faq.answer: Because yields on the assets Pendle wraps compressed. TVL fell from a September 2025 peak of $13.1 billion to roughly $1.5 billion in late April 2026, an 88 percent drawdown over seven months, alongside sUSDe APY moving from double digits to roughly 3.5 percent ([Real World Token Space](https://www.realworldtokenspace.com/research/2026-05-04-pendle-tvl-collapse-13b-to-15b-defi-fixed-income-structure-test)). Concentration made this worse: more than $4.6 billion of peak TVL, roughly 35 percent, came from Ethena yield bearing stablecoins.

Faq.question: What is Boros and how is it different from V2?
Faq.answer: Boros trades perpetual funding rates rather than spot yields. Each Yield Unit "represents the realized funding yield on 1 unit of notional, such as 1 ETH or 1 BTC, until expiry", and positions are structured as paying one interest stream and receiving another until maturity, which is the structure of an interest rate swap ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/08/06/pendle-lets-crypto-traders-bet-on-bitcoin-and-ether-funding-rates-with-boros-platform), [Boros Litepaper](https://docs.pendle.finance/boros-dev/LitePaper)).

Faq.question: Who governs Pendle and how do fees accrue?
Faq.answer: PENDLE holders lock into vePENDLE for up to two years, and gauge votes are snapshotted every Thursday at 00:00 UTC with a 5 percent default and 20 percent maximum pool cap ([Pendle docs, vePENDLE](https://docs.pendle.finance/ProtocolMechanics/Mechanisms/vePENDLE)). Since September 2025 the protocol routes 80 percent of holders revenue to sPENDLE, against annualised revenue of $23.97m ([DefiLlama Pendle](https://defillama.com/protocol/pendle)).

Faq.question: Is Pendle audited and is there a bug bounty?
Faq.answer: Pendle states its contracts have been audited by Ackee, Dedaub, Dingbats and top Code4rena wardens, with all reports published in the pendle-core-v2-public repository ([Pendle docs, Security](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/Security)). The Immunefi programme pays up to $250,000 for a critical smart contract finding with a $50,000 minimum and a mandatory proof of concept ([Immunefi Pendle](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/pendle/information/)).

Faq.question: Who is the counterparty if something goes wrong legally?
Faq.answer: The website and protocol are operated by Univerum Innovations Inc, an entity established under the laws of the Republic of Panama, with disputes routed to arbitration under the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ([Pendle Terms of Use](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/TermsOfUse)).

bull.claim: PT has become accepted collateral in the largest money markets, with more than $1.6 billion of PT supplied on Aave inside a single month and the PT-sUSDe-31JUL2025 cap raised from $85m to $1.3 billion (LlamaRisk on Aave).
Boros scaled fast, exceeding $250m open interest and roughly $7 billion cumulative notional volume within about four and a half months of launch (WEEX report of BlockBeats data).

The addressable pool is enormous relative to current penetration: average open interest in the funding rate market is about $150 billion and Boros accounts for only about 0.1 percent of it (WEEX report of BlockBeats data).

Pendle settled $45 billion of value for Principal Token holders during 2025 and is pushing into KYC compliant institutional distribution, with Galaxy Curator launching on Fireblocks on 16 July 2026 (Crypto Briefing via Bitget).

bear.claim: Demand is a derivative of underlying yield. TVL fell 88 percent from $13.1 billion in September 2025 to roughly $1.5 billion by late April 2026 as sUSDe APY dropped to roughly 3.5 percent (Real World Token Space).
Single-source concentration risk is structural: more than $4.6 billion of peak TVL, roughly 35 percent, came from Ethena stablecoins (Real World Token Space).

PT liquidity is thin relative to the size of the lending exposure it backs, which is why Chaos Labs built a killswitch that sets LTV to zero when 96 percent of PT liquidity concentration thresholds are breached (Chaos Labs). Its own example, PT-eUSDe-29MAY2025 reaching $200m of deposits in 24 hours, shows how fast that exposure can build.

Revenue is modest against the size of the token economy: annualised revenue is $23.97m on $935.95m of TVL as of 26 July 2026, and the January 2026 sPENDLE upgrade was itself described as the response to revenue compression (DefiLlama Pendle, Real World Token Space).

notional.LongDescription: Notional built fixed-rate, fixed-term lending and borrowing on Ethereum using fCash, a token representing a fixed amount of an asset at a fixed future date. A lender swaps cash for fCash at a rate set by the pool: 100 USDC lent for six months at 5 percent yields fCash of 100 × e^(0.05×0.5) = 102.53, and a borrower mints an offsetting positive and negative fCash pair against collateral ([Notional docs, using fCash](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-v3/fcash/using-fcash)). V3 removed the hard cliff at maturity by auto-converting matured fixed-rate debt into variable-rate debt, which allowed penalty-free rolls ([Introducing Notional V3](https://blog.notional.finance/introducing-notional-v3/)). This entity is not in steady state.
