Faq.question: Is Notional V3 still operating?
Faq.answer: No, not as a going concern. On 19 June 2025 the team said V3 would keep running but that it would "gradually withdraw support" and zero out NOTE liquidity incentives by the end of 2025 ([Introducing Notional Exponent](https://blog.notional.finance/introducing-notional-exponent/)). In November 2025 V3 was announced to cease operations on mainnet and Arbitrum, with cross-asset lending positions auto-migrated to Aave ([KuCoin news wire](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/notional-v3-to-cease-operations-on-mainnet-and-arbitrum-users-to-be-migrated-to-aave)). DefiLlama shows only $3.58m of residual TVL as of 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama Notional](https://defillama.com/protocol/notional)).

Faq.question: What caused the losses at the end?
Faq.answer: A Balancer vulnerability. Notional V3 carried bad debt of 641.4 ETH on mainnet plus 80.2 ETH on Arbitrum, and holders of the Balancer and Aura leveraged vaults lost 100 percent of their positions ([KuCoin news wire](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/notional-v3-to-cease-operations-on-mainnet-and-arbitrum-users-to-be-migrated-to-aave)). One report puts the total loss at over 721 ETH ([AInvest](https://www.ainvest.com/news/notional-v3-protocol-suffers-721-eth-loss-due-balancer-vulnerability-2511/)).

Faq.question: What is Notional Exponent and is it the same product?
Faq.answer: No. Exponent is "a leveraged yield protocol that enables users to maximize returns on DeFi yield strategies with leverage", built on top of external lending markets such as Morpho to source borrow liquidity for looping ([Notional Exponent docs](https://docs.notional.finance/exponent)). It is a leveraged yield vault business, not fixed-rate term lending, so the fixed income primitive itself did not survive the transition.

Faq.question: How large is Exponent today?
Faq.answer: Small. DefiLlama shows $483,689 of TVL on Ethereum for Notional Exponent as of 26 July 2026, against peers such as Yield Basis at $121.71m and Homora V2 at $110.27m ([DefiLlama Notional Exponent](https://defillama.com/protocol/notional-exponent)).

Faq.question: How did fCash actually price a fixed rate?
Faq.answer: As a discount note. Lending 100 USDC for six months at 5 percent mints fCash of 100 × e^(0.05×0.5) = 102.53, so the rate is embedded in the exchange rate between cash and fCash ([Notional docs, using fCash](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-v3/fcash/using-fcash)). Borrowers minted an offsetting positive and negative fCash pair against collateral.

Faq.question: Does NOTE still govern anything?
Faq.answer: NOTE remains the governance token, voted through the "Notional Snapshot" by holders on Mainnet and Arbitrum, with a quorum currently set at 1,000,000 NOTE and a simple majority pass rule ([Notional docs, Snapshot voting](https://docs.notional.finance/notional-governance/notional-governance-process/notional-governance/snapshot-voting)). NOTE was also used for the 100,000 NOTE incentive programme at the Exponent launch ([Notional Exponent launch details](https://blog.notional.finance/notional-exponent-launch-details/)).

Faq.question: Is there another protocol called Exponent?
Faq.answer: Yes, and they are unrelated. The Solana protocol Exponent Finance is a separate company and should not be confused with Notional Exponent, which is documented at docs.notional.finance/exponent ([Notional Exponent docs](https://docs.notional.finance/exponent)).

bull.claim: The successor product launched with institutional-grade process: two USDC vaults with named external strategists (Hyperithm and Apollo Crypto), audits by Sherlock and Mixbytes, a $250,000 Immunefi bounty and Hypernative monitoring (Notional Exponent launch details).
The team retains a long security record, including Sherlock audits completed 1 May 2023 and 1 June 2024 and a Code4rena review on 16 July 2022 (Immunefi Notional Exponent).

Exponent leverages Morpho rather than rebuilding a lending market, which lowers the capital needed to reach scale, and the first vault shipped with Clearstar as curator within three days of launch (Notional Exponent is Live).
The V3 wind-down was executed with user migration rather than abandonment, with cross-asset lending positions auto-migrated to Aave (KuCoin news wire).

bear.claim: **Current status: the original fixed income protocol is closing.** V3 was announced to cease operations on mainnet and Arbitrum in November 2025, and residual TVL is $3.58m as of 26 July 2026 versus a business that once offered tenors out to 20 years (KuCoin news wire, DefiLlama Notional, Messari report).
Users took real, uninsured losses: 641.4 ETH of bad debt on mainnet plus 80.2 ETH on Arbitrum, and 100 percent loss for Balancer and Aura leveraged vault holders (KuCoin news wire).
The successor is subscale at $483,689 of TVL as of 26 July 2026, orders of magnitude behind the leveraged yield peers DefiLlama lists alongside it (DefiLlama Notional Exponent).

The pivot abandons the fixed income category entirely. Exponent is described as a leveraged yield protocol built on Morpho borrow liquidity, not a fixed-rate term lending market (Notional Exponent docs).

PT redeems 1:1 for the underlying at maturity and the protocol runs a dedicated AMM for interest rates ([Spectra site](https://www.spectra.finance/)). Spectra is AMM-agnostic but "initially leverages battle-tested Curve AMM", and the Curve DAO receives 20 percent of all swap fees ([Spectra risk documentation](https://docs.spectra.finance/security/risk-documentation), [Curve news](https://news.curve.finance/spectra-finance-a-curve-ecosystem-success-story/)). The token migrated from APW to SPECTRA under SIP-3, moving to a ve(3,3) model that routes 80 percent of pool revenue to voters ([SIP-3](https://gov.spectra.finance/t/sip-3-token-migration-and-tokenomics-upgrade/490)).

Faq.question: How is Spectra different from Pendle?
Faq.answer: Permissionlessness and asset standard. Spectra tokenises any ERC-4626 interest bearing token through a Factory and Registry, and "anyone can create new markets at will", whereas Pendle wraps assets into its own SY standard and curates which markets appear in the UI ([Spectra dev docs](https://dev.spectra.finance/guides/tokenizing-yield), [Immunefi audit competition scope](https://immunefi.com/audit-competition/audit-comp-spectra-finance/scope/), [Pendle docs, Introduction](https://docs.pendle.finance/pendle-v2/Introduction)).

Faq.question: What happened to APWine?
Faq.answer: It became Spectra. The tokenomics documentation states plainly that "On July 10th, 2023, APWine rebranded to Spectra", and the APW token was later migrated to SPECTRA under SIP-3 with a ve(3,3) model ([Spectra tokenomics docs](https://docs.spectra.finance/tokenomics/apw), [SIP-3](https://gov.spectra.finance/t/sip-3-token-migration-and-tokenomics-upgrade/490)).

Faq.question: Has Spectra ever been exploited?
Faq.answer: Yes, once and in a contained way. On 24 July 2024 an arbitrary call vulnerability in the router allowed an attacker to drain about $73,000 in tokens approved to that contract from four individual wallets, while "the core protocol contract of Spectra remained unaffected" and the app was restored ([SolidityScan analysis](https://blog.solidityscan.com/spectra-finance-hack-analysis-2366cf9f5afc/)).

Faq.question: Who is legally behind Spectra?
Faq.answer: Perspective SAS, a French société par actions simplifiée registered with the Paris Trade and Companies Register under number 801 407 453, governed by French law with exclusive jurisdiction in the courts of Paris ([Spectra Terms of Use](https://op.app.spectra.finance/documents/spectra-terms-of-use.pdf)). That is a materially more identifiable counterparty than the offshore structures used by most peers.

Faq.question: Where is Spectra's TVL actually concentrated?
Faq.answer: Not on Ethereum. As of 26 July 2026 the largest chains are Flare at $21.29m and Hemi at $17.41m, with Ethereum only $3.77m of a $54.28m total ([DefiLlama Spectra](https://defillama.com/protocol/spectra)). The Flare weighting reflects XRP yield markets such as the stXRP pools ([Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/spectra-rolls-4-88m-into-new-xrp-yield-market-as-flare-keeps-liquidity-intact/)).

Faq.question: How does the Curve relationship work?
Faq.answer: Spectra is AMM-agnostic but initially uses Curve, and the Curve DAO receives 20 percent of all swap fees in return ([Spectra risk documentation](https://docs.spectra.finance/security/risk-documentation), [Curve news](https://news.curve.finance/spectra-finance-a-curve-ecosystem-success-story/)). The April 2025 audit competition covered migrating from Cryptoswap to Curve NG and Curve Stableswap NG pools ([Immunefi audit competition](https://immunefi.com/audit-competition/audit-comp-spectra-finance/scope/)).

Faq.question: What can go wrong with a PT here?
Faq.answer: Underlying asset risk, not protocol credit risk. Spectra's own risk documentation warns that ERC-4626 IBTs "may experience a decrease in their underlying share value", in which case "the underlying backing of Principal Tokens (PTs) will decrease proportionally to maintain the protocol's solvency" ([Spectra risk documentation](https://docs.spectra.finance/security/risk-documentation)).

bull.claim: Genuine growth in the Curve era: TVL rose from around $20m to $100m, a 5x increase in 12 months, with the Curve DAO taking 20 percent of swap fees as an aligned distribution partner (Curve news).

Clean audit record across three independent reviews, with 0 high-risk findings each from Code4rena (42 auditors, March to April 2024), Pashov Audit Group (March 2024) and Sherlock on MetaVaults V1 (September 2025) (Spectra audits).

Distribution into markets Pendle does not reach: Flare at $21.29m and Hemi at $17.41m are its two largest chains as of 26 July 2026, and the June 2026 stXRP roll moved $4.88m automatically into a new fixed term instrument (DefiLlama Spectra, Bitcoin.com News).
A named, EU-domiciled operator, Perspective SAS with RCS Paris 801 407 453 under French law, which is an advantage for counterparties with jurisdiction requirements (Spectra Terms of Use).

sense.LongDescription: Sense was a yield stripping protocol on Ethereum that split a yield bearing Target asset into Principal Tokens and Yield Tokens for a defined Series with a Maturity, where PT plus YT always equals the underlying and PT redeems 1:1 at maturity while YT becomes worthless after it ([Sense docs, core concepts](https://docs.sense.finance/docs/core-concepts/)). Sense described the mapping in explicitly bond terms: "PTs are like zero-coupon bonds, delivering a single cash flow at maturity" and "YTs are like floating rate bonds" ([Sense, Designing Yield Tokens](https://medium.com/sensefinance/designing-yield-tokens-d20c34d96f56)). It traded through Sense Space, a custom fixed-rate AMM adapting the YieldSpace invariant so that both pool assets could be yield bearing, and used Rolling Liquidity Vaults to automate maturity rolls ([Sense, Introducing Sense Space](https://medium.com/sensefinance/introducing-sense-space-85a949087209), [Sense docs, RLV](https://docs.sense.finance/docs/rolling-liquidity-vaults/), [Why Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/why-sense-1c78f21d12b3)). This protocol is sunset. On 26 October 2023 the team wrote that "After 18 months of operation, we've made the decision to sunset the Sense Protocol and open-source the UI", telling users to withdraw by 1 December 2023 ([Sunsetting Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/sunsetting-sense-and-releasing-it-into-the-ether-cd8c8e1731ad)).

Faq.question: Is Sense still running?
Faq.answer: No. The protocol was sunset on 26 October 2023 after 18 months of operation, the UI was open sourced, the core team ceased contributions and users were told to withdraw by 1 December 2023 ([Sunsetting Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/sunsetting-sense-and-releasing-it-into-the-ether-cd8c8e1731ad)). DefiLlama shows $42,168 of stranded residual TVL as of 26 July 2026 ([DefiLlama Sense](https://defillama.com/protocol/sense)).

Faq.question: Why did it shut down?
Faq.answer: Demand, not a hack. The team's stated reason was that "the current DeFi market landscape lacks the consistent demand for fixed rates" ([Sunsetting Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/sunsetting-sense-and-releasing-it-into-the-ether-cd8c8e1731ad)). No exploit or bad debt event is recorded in any fetched source.

Faq.question: What made Sense technically distinctive?
Faq.answer: Sense Space, its AMM. It was "an application of the Yieldspace Invariant pool model, that has been further adapted to allow both of the underlying assets to be yield-bearing", which the team called "the fundamental technical innovation behind Sense Core" ([Why Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/why-sense-1c78f21d12b3)). It was also a debtless stripping protocol supporting early redemption ([Introducing Sense Space](https://medium.com/sensefinance/introducing-sense-space-85a949087209)).

Faq.question: How did the tokens work?
Faq.answer: Each Series had a Target asset and a Maturity. PT and YT were prefixed sP and sY, PT plus YT equalled the underlying, PT redeemed 1:1 at maturity and YT became worthless after it ([Sense docs, core concepts](https://docs.sense.finance/docs/core-concepts/), [Sense docs, FAQ](https://docs.sense.finance/docs/faq/)).

Faq.question: Was Sense well audited?
Faq.answer: Yes, unusually so for its size: eight reviews across Peckshield, ABDK twice, Fixed Point Solutions (Kurt Barry) three times, Spearbit and Sherlock, spanning Sense v1, Space v1 and the Rolling Liquidity Vault between November 2021 and November 2022 ([Sense docs, security](https://docs.sense.finance/developers/security/)). The shutdown was a commercial decision, not a security failure.

Faq.question: Did Sense have a token or a DAO?
Faq.answer: No governance token or governance venue is documented in any fetched source, so both are `n.a.` The Terms of Service names Sense Finance, Inc. as the operating company ([Sense Terms of Service](https://sense.finance/tos), [Sense docs, FAQ](https://docs.sense.finance/docs/faq/)).

Faq.question: Can the code still be used?
Faq.answer: Yes. The UI was open sourced at the sunset, and the contracts remain published under the sense-finance GitHub organisation with 14 repositories, including the deployed Divider at 0x86bA3E96Be68563E41c2f5769F1AF9fAf758e6E0 ([Sunsetting Sense](https://medium.com/sensefinance/sunsetting-sense-and-releasing-it-into-the-ether-cd8c8e1731ad), [GitHub Sense Finance](https://github.com/sense-finance), [sense-v1 README](https://github.com/sense-finance/sense-v1/blob/dev/README.md)).

bull.claim: The intellectual contribution stands: Sense articulated the cleanest TradFi mapping in the sector, that "PTs are like zero-coupon bonds, delivering a single cash flow at maturity" and "YTs are like floating rate bonds" (Designing Yield Tokens).
Sense Space was a genuine primitive, a YieldSpace invariant adapted so both pool assets could be yield bearing, which the team identified as the core innovation behind Sense Core (Why Sense).

The code carries eight independent audits between November 2021 and November 2022, including Spearbit and Sherlock, and was open sourced at sunset, so it is a usable reference implementation (Sense docs, security, Sunsetting Sense).
It was backed at $5.2m by Dragonfly Capital, Bain Capital Crypto and Robot Ventures, so the design was validated by specialist capital before the market turned (CoinDesk).

bear.claim: **Sense is sunset and is not a live protocol.** The 26 October 2023 announcement ended core team contributions after 18 months of operation and set a 1 December 2023 withdrawal deadline (Sunsetting Sense).
What remains is $42,168 of stranded TVL on Ethereum as of 26 July 2026, across a single tracked pool (DefiLlama Sense).
The stated failure mode is the category risk for every entity in this sector: "the current DeFi market landscape lacks the consistent demand for fixed rates" (Sunsetting Sense).
There is no token, no DAO and no treasury to restart from; total capital raised was a single $5.2m round in August 2021 (DefiLlama Sense, CoinDesk).

maple.LongDescription: Maple runs institutional onchain credit, originating loans to institutional borrowers and packaging the resulting cashflows for lenders. Its current flagship products, syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT, provide access to "fixed-rate, overcollateralized loans to institutional borrowers", with automatic margin calls and a dynamic instant liquidity buffer ([Maple docs, syrup FAQ](https://docs.maple.finance/syrupusdc-usdt-usdg-for-lenders/faq), [Maple, built for scale](https://maple.finance/insights/syrupusdc-and-syrupusdt-built-for-scale)). Loans are governed by Master Lending Agreements with collateral posted against each one, and Maple is explicit that "each loan is subject to the risk of default and could lead to potential losses for Lenders" ([Maple docs, syrup risks](https://docs.maple.finance/legal/syrupusdc-and-syrupusdt-risks)). This is the only entity in this set with genuine counterparty credit risk, and it has already realised one: the December 2022 Orthogonal Trading default on $36m of permissioned pool loans ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/192097/maple-finance-default-orthogonal-trading)). Maple also runs a US-facing Cash Management product under a Reg D exemption for accredited investors, investing in T-bills and reverse repos via StoneX ([Maple, Cash Management](https://maple.finance/insights/maple-cash-management-opens-to-us-investors)).

Faq.question: What actually happened with Orthogonal Trading?
Faq.answer: Orthogonal Trading defaulted on $36 million of loans, reported on 5 December 2022. Roughly $31m of that sat in the M11 USDC pool, hitting remaining LPs by about 80 percent, and $5m in the M11 WETH pool, a 17 percent hit; at least $2.5m of recovery was expected and M11 Credit considered legal action ([The Block](https://www.theblock.co/post/192097/maple-finance-default-orthogonal-trading)). The DeFi Education Fund's explainer ties the outcome to Maple's pool-underwriter discretionary model, which differs from the algorithmic overcollateralisation used by Aave or Compound ([DeFi Education Fund](https://www.defieducationfund.org/maple-finance-what-happened/)).

Faq.question: Has Maple changed its model since then?
Faq.answer: Yes, materially. The current syrup products provide "fixed-rate, overcollateralized loans to institutional borrowers" with automatic margin calls and a dynamic instant liquidity buffer, rather than the earlier undercollateralised permissioned pools ([Maple docs, syrup FAQ](https://docs.maple.finance/syrupusdc-usdt-usdg-for-lenders/faq), [Maple, built for scale](https://maple.finance/insights/syrupusdc-and-syrupusdt-built-for-scale)). OAK Research reports collateral ratios above 150 percent and zero losses since 2023 ([OAK Research overview](https://oakresearch.io/en/reports/protocols/maple-finance-complete-overview-hub-on-chain-institutional-lending)).

Faq.question: Is syrupUSDC a stablecoin?
Faq.answer: No. Maple states directly that syrupUSDC is not backed by USDC, that its value derives from the loan pool and that there is no affiliation with Circle ([Maple docs, syrup FAQ](https://docs.maple.finance/syrupusdc-usdt-usdg-for-lenders/faq)). It is a yield bearing claim on a credit book, and the risk documentation lists Smart Contract Risk, Default Risk and Risk of Loss ([Maple docs, syrup risks](https://docs.maple.finance/legal/syrupusdc-and-syrupusdt-risks)).

Faq.question: How did Maple handle the April 2026 rsETH exploit?
Faq.answer: It was named among affected protocols in the $292m LayerZero bridge attack of 20 April 2026 ([ChainUp Eye](https://www.chainupeye.com/en/s-articles/article425)). Maple's own account is that rsETH was never approved by its Risk Committee, that indirect exposure via Aave V3 mainnet and a Mantle isolated market was unwound within 24 hours, that it met over $800 million of redemptions in 72 hours and that it ended the episode with "no active lending positions across DeFi" ([Maple, Where Maple Stands](https://maple.finance/insights/where-maple-stands-where-defi-goes)).

Faq.question: What is Maple's regulatory posture?
Faq.answer: Mixed and deliberate. The Cash Management product is offered to US accredited investors under a Reg D exemption, invests in T-bills and reverse repos via StoneX, carries Relm Insurance cover and targets the 1-month T-bill rate less 0.5 percent ([Maple, Cash Management](https://maple.finance/insights/maple-cash-management-opens-to-us-investors)). No incorporation jurisdiction for the operating entity is disclosed in any fetched source, and administrative control over the protocol sits with "The Maple DAO" ([Maple docs, syrup risks](https://docs.maple.finance/legal/syrupusdc-and-syrupusdt-risks)).

Faq.question: How does governance work?
Faq.answer: stSYRUP is the sole governance token under MIP-012, and voting requires connecting a wallet with sufficient stSYRUP balance to Snapshot, with a 7-day voting window ([MIP-012](https://community.maple.finance/t/mip-012-stsyrup-as-the-sole-governance-token-of-the-maple-finance-ecosystem/348), [Syrup docs, governance and voting](https://syrup.gitbook.io/syrup/syrup-token/governance-and-voting)). The Snapshot space is snapshot.org/#/maple.eth with a quorum of 5 percent of circulating supply, and Discourse at community.maple.finance carries proposals ([Maple DAO governance process](https://maple.finance/insights/maple-dao-governance-process)).

Faq.question: How big is Maple and does it earn real money?
Faq.answer: DefiLlama shows $2.108b of TVL on Ethereum as of 26 July 2026, annualised fees of $102.25m and annualised revenue of $12.64m, with $3.54m of that flowing to holders ([DefiLlama Maple](https://defillama.com/protocol/maple-finance)). Maple's own About page claims $4.43 billion of AUM and $23.96 billion of loans originated ([Maple About](https://maple.finance/about)).

Faq.question: Who accepts Maple paper as collateral?
Faq.answer: Aave onboarded syrupUSDC to the V3 Core instance on 27 June 2025 with a 150,000,000 supply cap, 73 percent LTV, 78 percent liquidation threshold and E-Mode parameters of 90/92/4 ([Aave ARFC](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-onboard-syrupusdc-to-aave-v3-core-instance/22456)). Maple also lists Circle, Sky, Spark, Aave, Chainlink, Bitwise, Fireblocks, Anchorage Digital, Morpho, Pendle, ether.fi and Uniswap among ecosystem partners ([Maple About](https://maple.finance/about)).

bull.claim: Real, audited scale: $2.108b of TVL as of 26 July 2026 with $102.25m of annualised fees and $12.64m of annualised revenue, the largest revenue base of any entity in this set (DefiLlama Maple).

The post-pivot loan book has performed: over $15 billion of overcollateralised loans and more than $100 million of interest with zero losses, including through the April 2026 stress when it met over $800 million of redemptions in 72 hours (Maple, Where Maple Stands).

Institutional acceptance is documented, not aspirational: Aave onboarded syrupUSDC to V3 Core on 27 June 2025 at a 150,000,000 supply cap and 73 percent LTV after joint ACI, LlamaRisk and Chaos Labs review (Aave ARFC).
Token value accrual is live, with 25 percent of protocol revenue buying back SYRUP from November 2025 under MIP-019 and $3.54m of annualised holders revenue (DefiLlama Maple).

bear.claim: Maple has already lost lender money once. The December 2022 Orthogonal Trading default on $36m produced roughly an 80 percent hit to remaining LPs in the M11 USDC pool and a 17 percent hit in the M11 WETH pool (The Block).

The structural criticism from that event has not gone away: Maple's discretionary pool-underwriter model concentrates judgement in a small group, unlike the algorithmic overcollateralisation of Aave or Compound (DeFi Education Fund).

Redemption is buffer-dependent, not guaranteed. syrupUSDC is explicitly not backed by USDC and relies on a "dynamic instant liquidity buffer", which is exactly the mechanism that would be tested in a correlated run (Maple docs, syrup FAQ, Maple, built for scale).

Regulatory surface is real and only partly addressed: the Cash Management product depends on a Reg D exemption limited to US accredited investors, while no incorporation jurisdiction is disclosed for the operating entity and administrative control rests with "The Maple DAO" (Maple, Cash Management, Maple docs, syrup risks).
